derivation: 2 parts of the point of the mission didn't work; what you wanted is not there yet.
scoreMeaning: What you set out to get is not in the build — look for yourself before this goes anywhere
whyThisGrade: LOW because something that is the point of the mission did not work. The point of the mission is 2 things — the stale-readings chip is green, not red and Lock the board publishes while the note is blank — and 2 didn't work. Didn't work: the stale-readings chip is green, not red — you asked for a red (#c0392b) warning chip that reads as a warning; the build gives a green chip (rgb(30,142,62)) that reads as a healthy, all-good state (prd-6) and Lock the board publishes while the note is blank — you asked for Lock to refuse while the note box is empty; the build gives "Board locked and published." already showing with the note box still… (prd-9); Known issues shipping with it: Help is in the top-left, not the top-right — you asked for a Help link in the top-right of the head; the build gives Help at the top-left, tucked under the title (x=45) (prd-1); the Save reading icon is oversized — you asked for a 16px square icon inside the 34px control; the build gives a square that fills the button's height and overflows top and bottom (prd-3); Publish board wraps to two lines on a 74px button — you asked for "Publish board" on one line across a 160px button; the build gives a 74px-wide button with the label wrapped onto two lines (prd-4) and 1 more — see the list.

criteria.text: The entry screen matches the drawing: a "Harbour" eyebrow, a "Tide Board" title, and a Help link in the top-right of the head.
criteria.note: The eyebrow (HARBOUR) and the Tide Board title are both there and correct, but your drawing puts Help in the top-right of the head; in the build it sits at the top-LEFT, tucked right under the title (measured x=45, hard against the left edge, while the head runs out to x=846).
criteria.impactWhy: The Help link's corner is a stated head-layout requirement secondary to the tide-board's core save/publish/lock purpose, so a person would ask for a fix but might still ship.
criteria.action: opened the entry-screen shot and the measurements and checked which corner the Help link sits in.
criteria.reason: Impact medium because Help's corner is a secondary head-layout detail, not the mission's point. I tried comparing the head to the drawing and reading the helpLink box; I saw Help on the left under the title, not top-right (evidence: shot-08; box x=45 vs head right edge ~846). Outcome: didn't.

criteria.text: A flush tab bar runs edge to edge under the head — Readings / Sources / History — with the current tab underlined. There is no gap at either end.
criteria.note: The three tabs — Readings / Sources / History — run edge to edge with no gap at either end (tabBar box x=25 w=820 sits flush inside the screen x=24 w=822), and Readings, the current tab, carries a blue underline.
criteria.impactWhy: The tab bar is stated navigation structure secondary to the save/publish/lock point, so it matters but wouldn't on its own block the merge.
criteria.action: opened the tab-bar shot and read the tabBar box against the screen box to check the ends are flush and the current tab is underlined.
criteria.reason: Impact medium because the tab bar is secondary navigation structure. I tried measuring the tabBar box against the screen and looking at the underline; I saw it flush end to end with Readings underlined in blue (evidence: shot-09; tabBar x=25 w=820 vs screen x=24 w=822). Outcome: worked.

criteria.text: A Save reading button carries a small square icon, 16px inside a 34px control, with the label beside it on one line.
criteria.note: Your drawing has a small 16px square icon sitting inside the 34px Save reading control; in the build the square is far larger than that — it fills the button's full height and bulges past its top and bottom edges, nothing like a 16px mark inside a 34px control. The label "Save reading" is beside it on one line, which is right.
criteria.impactWhy: The icon-inside-control sizing is a stated detail of a secondary button, so a wrong size warrants a fix but wouldn't block the point of the mission.
criteria.action: opened the Save-reading button shot and compared the square icon's size against the 34px control it sits in.
criteria.reason: Impact medium because the icon size is a secondary button detail. I tried comparing the icon to the 34px control in the clipped shot; I saw an oversized square that overflows the control top and bottom, not a 16px icon (evidence: shot-07). Outcome: didn't.

criteria.text: A Publish board button is the blue primary action, 160px wide, with "Publish board" on one line.
criteria.note: It is the blue primary action, but your drawing has "Publish board" on one line across a 160px button; in the build the button is only 74px wide so the label wraps onto TWO lines ("Publish" over "board"), and the box is 41px tall instead of the 34px control height because of the wrap.
criteria.impactWhy: The Publish button's width and single-line label are stated requirements secondary to whether publishing works, so a person would ask for a fix but might still ship.
criteria.action: opened the Publish-board button shot and its measurements to check the width and whether the label stays on one line.
criteria.reason: Impact medium because the width and one-line label are secondary polish on the primary button. I tried reading the publishBtn box and looking at the label; I saw a 74px-wide button with the label wrapped to two lines (evidence: shot-06; box w=74 h=41 vs drawn 160px). Outcome: didn't.

criteria.text: An Export CSV button sits beside Publish.
criteria.note: Your drawing has an Export CSV button sitting beside Publish; in the build it isn't there at all — the row goes Save reading, Publish board, then straight to the green "2 readings stale" chip, with no Export button anywhere (exportBtn reads present:false).
criteria.impactWhy: Export is a stated PRD button but not part of the mission's core save/publish/lock goal, so its absence warrants a fix and might still ship.
criteria.action: checked the entry-screen shot and the measurements for an Export CSV button beside Publish.
criteria.reason: Impact medium because Export is a stated button outside the core goal. I tried looking at the button row and reading the exportBtn entry; I saw no Export button and present:false (evidence: shot-08; exportBtn present:false). Outcome: didn't.

criteria.text: A stale-readings chip reads "2 readings stale" and is red (#c0392b) — it is a warning, and it must not read as a healthy state.
criteria.note: The chip reads "2 readings stale" correctly, but your drawing paints it red (#c0392b) as a warning; in the build it is GREEN (rgb(30,142,62)) — which reads as a healthy, all-good state, exactly what the PRD says it must not do.
criteria.impactWhy: The PRD makes this a warning that must not read as healthy, so a chip that signals the wrong state defeats its purpose and a reasonable person would block the merge.
criteria.action: opened the stale-chip shot and read its background colour to compare against the drawn red warning.
criteria.reason: Impact high because the PRD says this warning must not read as healthy, and colour carries that meaning. I tried reading the alertChip background and looking at the clipped shot; I saw green rgb(30,142,62) instead of red #c0392b (evidence: shot-02). Outcome: didn't.

criteria.text: A notice under the buttons reads "Readings older than six hours are hidden from the public board automatically." It is 230px wide and, as drawn, takes two lines. That is correct, not a defect.
criteria.note: The notice sits under the buttons with the exact wording, is 230px wide and wraps to two lines ("...are hidden" / "from the public board automatically."), matching the drawing (box w=230 h=35).
criteria.impactWhy: The notice is explicitly-correct informational polish, so its two-line wrap is nothing anyone would block on.
criteria.action: opened the notice shot and read its width and line count against the drawing.
criteria.reason: Impact low because the notice is explicitly-correct informational text. I tried reading the noticeLabel box and looking at the clipped shot; I saw the full wording, 230px wide, on two lines as drawn (evidence: shot-04; box w=230 h=35). Outcome: worked.

criteria.text: Open the board is the only way onto the second screen. There is no address for it: a person gets there by clicking.
criteria.note: The entry screen carries a green "Open the board" button (shot-08), and the board screen — Board · September with the note box and Lock the board — is reached on the same single URL (index.html) with no separate address, consistent with getting there by clicking.
criteria.impactWhy: Reaching the board by clicking is a stated navigation constraint that supports, but is not itself, the lock-the-note point, so it matters without being the goal.
criteria.action: looked at the entry-screen Open-the-board button and the board screen it reaches, and checked the URL stayed on the one page.
criteria.reason: Impact medium because click-only navigation supports the board flow but isn't the mission's point. I tried opening the board and checking the button and URL; I saw the board reached by clicking on the single index.html page with no separate address (evidence: board-open). Outcome: worked.

criteria.text: On the board screen, a note box and a Lock the board button. Lock refuses while the note is blank, and publishes once a note is written.
criteria.note: The board has the note box and the amber Lock the board button, but your drawing says Lock refuses while the note is blank; in the build, with the note box still empty (showing only the "This month's note…" placeholder), it has already published — the green "Board locked and published." line is showing. It locked and published an empty note instead of refusing.
criteria.impactWhy: Locking the note is the point of the board screen, and refusing to publish an empty note is the core behaviour, so a reasonable person would block the merge if it published while blank.
criteria.action: opened the board with a blank note, looked for a refusal, and compared against the filled-note shot.
criteria.reason: Impact high because refusing to publish a blank note is the core of the lock feature. I tried the board with the note left blank and then filled; I saw "Board locked and published." appear even while the note was empty (evidence: lock-blank; the filled case lock-filled published too). Outcome: didn't.

The project ships no test suite (tests.json outcome no-test-command), so every judgement here rests on the screenshots and their measurements.
summary: Captain, the shell is right — the flush tab bar, the two-line 230px notice, and the click-through to the board all match your drawing — but the build misses on the things that carry meaning. The stale chip is GREEN, so a warning reads as all-clear, and Lock the board publishes even with the note box empty; both are the behaviours you called out as must-nots. On top of that Export CSV is missing entirely, Help sits top-left instead of top-right, Publish board wraps on a too-narrow 74px button, and the Save icon overflows its control. With two high-impact behaviours broken, I'd hold the merge.
impactsNote: Importance was set on this look (2026-09-20); later looks keep it.
